final_candidates.decision_summary: Hydrophobic substitution in HA2 stem may improve packing and thermostability without affecting receptor binding or fusion.
Conservative hydrophobic-to-hydrophobic change in HA2 maintains structure and may slightly enhance stability with minimal risk.
Proline may rigidify a flexible HA2 loop, potentially increasing thermostability while preserving distant receptor-binding residues.

stop_reason.detail: Sufficient candidate refinement achieved within limited self-iteration; further rounds without external evidence are unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Ala-to-Ser at a strained loop in the HA1 body can form additional backbone/side-chain hydrogen bonds and reduce local unfolding; this site is away from the receptor-binding pocket and is compatible with H5 HA cell entry.
Serine may add hydrogen bonding but is near receptor-binding site; lower priority due to potential impact on cell entry.
Also in the receptor-binding domain; introducing a polar serine may disrupt local packing or binding, with low likelihood of improving global stability.

rejection.reason: Also in the receptor-binding domain; introducing a polar serine may disrupt local packing or binding, with low likelihood of improving global stability.

history.rationale: Position 403 corresponds to HA2 K58 in the stem trimer periphery; introducing Ile improves hydrophobic packing at the trimer interface and is frequently associated with increased HA thermostability while keeping the fusion machinery intact.
Removing charged lysine may affect salt bridges at HA2 interface; less confident for stability improvement.
Removing a charged residue in HA2 could destabilize salt bridges or surface contacts, likely harming folding stability.

rejection.reason: Removing a charged residue in HA2 could destabilize salt bridges or surface contacts, likely harming folding stability.

history.rationale: Glycine in the exposed 140-loop allows excessive backbone flexibility; proline substitution reduces conformational entropy and should raise the unfolding barrier with only local effect on antigenic surface.
Proline in a loop can reduce backbone entropy and increase thermostability, though may affect loop dynamics.
Position 146 lies in the HA1 receptor-binding domain; proline substitution could perturb receptor binding, conflicting with the requirement to preserve cell entry.

rejection.reason: Position 146 lies in the HA1 receptor-binding domain; proline substitution could perturb receptor binding, conflicting with the requirement to preserve cell entry.

history.rationale: A conservative isoleucine-to-leucine change in the HA2 stem may slightly increase buried hydrophobic contact while preserving the underlying helix geometry.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution in HA2 may enhance core packing and improve folding stability.
Conservative substitution in HA2 that preserves hydrophobic character, low risk but also limited expected stabilization.

Substituting leucine with phenylalanine at a putative hydrophobic packing site in HA2 can fill a cavity and stabilize the prefusion trimer; it is distal to the receptor-binding and fusion peptide regions.
Aromatic phenylalanine at HA2 position adds hydrophobic packing and likely increases thermal stability without disrupting fusion.
Located in the HA2 stem, away from the receptor-binding domain and fusion peptide; potentially improves hydrophobic packing without obvious effects on cell entry.
Glycine to proline in a flexible loop of HA2 (likely between fusion peptide and helix) may rigidify the loop and increase thermostability without altering key binding or fusion residues.
